title: Army Tuition Assistance via ArmyIgnitED
eligibility: Eligible serving Army Soldiers
description: Army funding can help pay tuition for approved classes taken outside duty hours. Apply through ArmyIgnitED before starting.
caveats: Supervisor/commander representative approval required since March 19, 2026. First-time training and decision-support tool required. TA/CA share overall fiscal-year ceiling; confirm available funding in ArmyIgnitED.

title: Army Credentialing Assistance
eligibility: Eligible Army enlisted Soldiers and warrant officers
description: Army funding can help you earn approved civilian job certifications or licenses. Your rank, funding limits, and approval requirements matter.
caveats: Commissioned officers ineligible after March 19, 2026, apart from stated grandfathering. Supervisor approval; combined TA/CA ceiling $4,500. Course/exam requirements and recoupment apply.

title: Army Career Skills Program
eligibility: Transitioning Soldiers expecting honorable or general under honorable separation
description: Build civilian job skills before leaving the Army through approved training, an apprenticeship, or an internship.
caveats: Typically last 180 days eligibility window; actual authorized duration varies by rank/category. IDES/SRU timing can differ; ask CSP counselor. Not automatic permission or job guarantee.

title: Army Recovery Care Coordination
eligibility: Qualifying seriously wounded, ill or injured Soldiers; SRU Soldiers and certain transitioning medical retirees
description: A recovery coordinator helps eligible wounded, ill, or injured Soldiers organize support and plan the move back to duty or civilian life.
caveats: Clinical/program criteria apply; disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Includes stated TDRL/SRU categories.

title: Army MWR Leisure Travel Services
eligibility: Eligible Army MWR patrons including active duty and retirees
description: Local travel offices offer discounted ticket and leisure travel options.
caveats: Vendor-specific tickets have stricter eligibility than general MWR access. Confirm local inventory and ID; 10% VA/VHIC does not qualify for every military salute offer.

title: Army MWR retail recreation
eligibility: Active duty, retirees and qualifying service-connected disabled veterans
description: Access to eligible recreation, lodging, golf, bowling, equipment rental and other MWR activities.
caveats: Facility, installation access and patron-category rules apply. Benefits may involve fees; eligibility is not free admission to all facilities.

title: Microsoft Software and Systems Academy (MSSA)
eligibility: Transitioning active duty; veterans; retirees; Guard/Reserve
description: A free, full-time 17-week technology training program from Microsoft. It helps eligible service members and veterans prepare for jobs in cloud computing, software development, or cybersecurity.
caveats: Admissions and prerequisites apply. Service members generally within six months of separation; no guaranteed job. Next listed April 2027 cohort application window: November 16–30, 2026.

title: Veteran Readiness and Employment (VR&E)
eligibility: Veterans with VA service-connected rating 10%+; some active duty applicants
description: VA helps you plan for work, train for a suitable career, or live more independently when a service-connected disability creates barriers.
caveats: 10% allows application, not automatic entitlement: serious employment handicap generally needed at 10%; counselor decides. Dishonorable discharge ordinarily excludes.

title: Army Emergency Relief
eligibility: Active duty and medically or otherwise eligible retired Soldiers and families
description: Army Emergency Relief may help cover an urgent bill or essential expense with a grant, an interest-free loan, or both. A grant does not need to be repaid; a loan does.
caveats: Branch and status restrictions; individualized assessment. Not all awards are grants.

title: Army Career Skills Support grants
eligibility: Retiring or separating Soldiers in Army Career Skills Program
description: Location-dependent grants to reduce transition training costs.
caveats: CSP participation and program rules required; awards vary.

title: MSSA Europe
eligibility: Eligible US or UK service members and veterans in Europe
description: MSSA training offered in Central European Time.
caveats: Admissions apply; listed April 5–July 30, 2027 cohort accepts applications November 16–30, 2026.

title: SkillBridge
eligibility: Transitioning active duty
description: Get civilian work experience or job training near the end of your military service. Your command must approve participation before you start.
caveats: Written command approval required; service policies can limit participation duration. Participation and employment are not guaranteed.

title: Post-9/11 GI Bill
eligibility: Qualifying active duty or veterans with qualifying service and discharge
description: Use earned military education benefits to help pay for approved college or job training. Housing and book payments depend on your situation.
caveats: Generally requires honorable discharge for veterans; general under honorable alone is not sufficient for this GI Bill. Qualifying service and approved program required; active-duty housing allowance rules differ.

title: Yellow Ribbon Program
eligibility: 100% Post-9/11 GI Bill benefit level; participating school
description: Some schools and VA share extra tuition costs that your Post-9/11 GI Bill does not cover. You must qualify at the full GI Bill benefit level.
caveats: School capacity and agreement limit awards; 100% GI Bill eligibility is different from a 100% disability rating.

title: Rogers STEM Scholarship
eligibility: Eligible Post-9/11 GI Bill veterans or Fry Scholars in qualifying STEM study
description: Extra education support for eligible students finishing certain science, technology, engineering, or math programs when their GI Bill benefits are running low.
caveats: Award is not automatic; qualifying degree, credits and remaining entitlement rules apply.

title: GI Bill foreign-school study
eligibility: Eligible GI Bill beneficiaries
description: Use earned education benefits at approved foreign programs.
caveats: VA must approve the school and program; confirm coverage before enrolling.

title: VA disability compensation
eligibility: Veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities rated 10%+
description: A monthly, tax-free VA payment for qualifying disabilities connected to your military service.
caveats: VA and military disability ratings are separate. Character-of-service rules apply; active-duty pay affects payment.

title: Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC)
eligibility: Military retirees with combat-related VA disability 10%+
description: Some retirees with combat-related disabilities can recover part of the military retired pay reduced because they also receive VA disability pay.
caveats: Apply to service branch; combat-related approval required. Chapter 61 limitations and retired-pay offsets affect amount.

title: Army Wounded Warrior Comfort Grants
eligibility: Qualifying medically evacuated Soldiers
description: Immediate hospitalization grant for eligible medical evacuation circumstances.
caveats: Specific evacuation and hospitalization criteria apply; ask AER office.

title: VA clothing allowance
eligibility: Veterans whose service-connected device or skin medication damages clothing
description: An annual VA payment may help replace clothes damaged by a qualifying disability device or prescribed skin medicine.
caveats: Qualifying device/medicine and application rules; August 1 annual qualification deadline. Rating percentage alone does not qualify.

title: VA automobile allowance and adaptive equipment
eligibility: Veterans or service members with specific service-connected impairments
description: VA may help you buy or adapt a vehicle if you have a specific qualifying disability. Get approval before making the purchase.
geographic_scope: United States; contact VA for overseas use
caveats: Approval required before purchase. Specific limb, vision, burn, ALS or joint criteria; 10% alone insufficient.

title: Specially Adapted Housing (SAH)
eligibility: Veterans or service members with specified service-connected impairments
description: A VA grant may help you build, buy, or change a permanent home to make it accessible for certain severe service-connected disabilities.
geographic_scope: United States; overseas application requires confirmation
caveats: Specific disability and ownership criteria; no blanket eligibility at 10% or 30%.

title: Special Home Adaptation (SHA)
eligibility: Veterans or service members with specified service-connected impairments
description: A VA grant may help pay for home changes needed for certain qualifying service-connected disabilities.
geographic_scope: United States; overseas application requires confirmation
caveats: Qualifying disabilities and ownership rules apply.

title: Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA)
eligibility: SAH/SHA-eligible people temporarily living with family
description: If you qualify for an adapted-housing grant but temporarily live in a family member’s home, VA may help pay for needed changes there.
geographic_scope: United States; overseas application requires confirmation
caveats: Must meet SAH or SHA eligibility; separate caps apply.

title: Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA)
eligibility: Eligible veterans/service members with prescribed medical access needs
description: VA may help pay for medically necessary home changes, such as improving access to entrances, bathrooms, or essential facilities.
caveats: Medical justification and application required; lifetime limits and exclusions apply.

title: VA home loan funding-fee exemption
eligibility: VA compensation recipients or eligible recipients paid active/retired pay instead; other exceptions
description: Eligible borrowers can skip the VA home-loan funding fee. This does not remove other closing costs or the need to qualify for the loan.
caveats: Pre-discharge proposed rating must precede closing. Loan underwriting, COE and other costs still apply.

title: VA-backed home loans
eligibility: Qualifying service members and veterans with COE
description: Home financing that may avoid down payment and monthly mortgage insurance.
caveats: Credit, income, occupancy, service and discharge requirements; not a cash grant.

title: TRICARE medical retirement
eligibility: Members on Temporary or Permanent Disability Retirement List
description: If the military medically retires you, you and eligible family members may have retiree TRICARE health coverage options.
caveats: Enroll within 90 days of retirement. DoD disability rating differs from VA rating; 30% VA alone does not establish retirement.

title: Foreign Medical Program
eligibility: Veterans with VA-rated service-connected conditions abroad
description: While living or traveling abroad, VA may pay for qualifying treatment related to your service-connected conditions. It is not full overseas health insurance.
caveats: Not comprehensive overseas health insurance; unrelated care and travel costs generally excluded.

title: VA travel reimbursement
eligibility: Eligible VA patients; includes service-connected care below 30%
description: VA may repay some travel costs for qualifying medical appointments. Eligibility depends on your rating, the treatment, and other rules.
caveats: 30% VA can qualify on broader grounds; below 30% may qualify for service-connected treatment. Filing and deductible rules apply.

title: Wounded Warrior Project registration
eligibility: Post-9/11 service members in good standing and honorably discharged veterans; other discharges reviewed case by case. Physical or combat injury is not required by the current registration FAQ.
description: Free connection events and wellness, benefits and transition support help you find useful services and community.
geographic_scope: United States; ask about overseas access
caveats: Registration verification applies; individual programs can add clinical criteria. In-person and virtual options vary.

title: VA benefit tax exclusions
eligibility: Recipients of qualifying VA benefits
description: VA disability compensation and qualifying education or adaptation benefits are excluded from federal taxable income.
caveats: Military retirement pay has separate tax treatment; state rules vary.

title: Military PCS moving-expense deduction
eligibility: Active-duty members moving under qualifying military orders
description: Deduction for eligible unreimbursed moving costs.
geographic_scope: US tax filers; domestic / overseas moves
caveats: No double deduction for government-covered expenses; timing and PCS rules apply.

title: MilTax
eligibility: Eligible military members and families; recently separated/retired within 365 days
description: Free military-focused tax preparation software and consultant support.
caveats: Eligibility and annual software availability apply; verify current supported state-return count.

title: SCRA interest-rate and lease protections
eligibility: Qualifying active-duty service members
description: Military-service legal protections may lower interest on qualifying debt you had before service or let you end certain leases after eligible orders.
caveats: Written notice, orders and deadlines may apply; not a general 6% cap on new loans.

title: National parks military annual pass
eligibility: Current US military and dependents
description: Free annual pass covering entrance and standard day-use fees at participating federal lands.
caveats: Proof required; camping, reservations and concession fees generally not covered.

title: National parks veteran lifetime pass
eligibility: US veterans with accepted proof
description: Lifetime entrance and standard day-use access to participating federal lands.
caveats: Accepted identity proof required. Source does not expressly resolve dishonorable eligibility; mark provider verification required.

title: Blue Star Museums
eligibility: Active duty; Guard/Reserve; eligible families
description: Seasonal free admission for ID holder and up to five family members at participating museums.
caveats: Armed Forces Day through Labor Day; 2026 season has ended. Retirees/veterans not included solely by that status.

title: Vet Tix
eligibility: Currently serving military; honorably discharged veterans and retirees; eligible survivors
description: Donated event tickets through verified membership.
caveats: Delivery fees, limited inventory and lotteries may apply. Dishonorable veterans excluded by stated honorable-service eligibility.

title: Space-Available military travel
eligibility: Eligible active duty on leave; military retirees; certain permanently totally disabled veterans
description: You may be able to use an empty seat on a military flight. Availability and your travel category decide whether you can fly; a seat is never guaranteed.
caveats: Seats never guaranteed. 10% or 30% VA alone insufficient; nonretired total-disability travel has destination restrictions. Check terminal.

title: American Airlines military baggage
eligibility: Active US military; certain dependents on orders
description: Qualifying free checked-bag allowance on eligible American itineraries.
caveats: ID, orders, itinerary and weight limits apply. Codeshare restrictions; ordinary veteran status alone insufficient.

title: American Airlines Group 1 boarding
eligibility: Active duty with military ID
description: Board in Group 1 under American’s military policy.
caveats: Active duty status required; not a universal veteran or all-airlines entitlement.

title: Home Depot military discount
eligibility: Active service members, veterans and spouses with verification
description: 10% off eligible purchases through verified account.
caveats: Product exclusions and verification apply; dishonorable-discharge acceptance not established by reviewed page.

title: Lowe’s military discount
eligibility: Eligible current/former service members and verified spouses
description: 10% off eligible full-price products.
caveats: Dishonorable discharges excluded. Sale items, major appliances, many commodities and services excluded.

title: Commissary, exchange and selected MWR privileges
eligibility: Active duty; retirees; eligible service-connected disabled veterans
description: Access to eligible military retail facilities, including certain VA-rated veterans.
geographic_scope: United States / overseas subject to host-nation rules
caveats: Base access, VHIC/ID and overseas agreements apply; retail privileges do not mean every MWR service is available.

title: Discharge upgrade and VA character-of-discharge review
eligibility: Former members with adverse discharges
description: Routes to request review of discharge status or eligibility for VA purposes.
caveats: OTH is different from dishonorable. VA review does not change military discharge; statutory bars can remain. Separate honorable service periods may qualify.

title: Texas disabled-veteran partial property-tax exemption
eligibility: Qualifying disabled veterans with VA rating 10%+ and eligible Texas property
description: A qualifying VA rating can reduce the taxable value of eligible Texas property. This is a reduction in the value used to calculate tax, not a cash payment.
caveats: This reduces assessed value, not tax owed dollar for dollar. Apply to county appraisal district; ownership and other requirements apply.

title: Texas 100% disabled-veteran homestead exemption
eligibility: Qualifying Texas homestead owners with 100% VA disability compensation and 100% rating or individual unemployability
description: Potential full exemption on qualifying residence homestead.
caveats: 10% or 30% alone does not qualify. Homestead and documentation requirements apply.

title: Texas Hazlewood Act
eligibility: Qualifying Texas-connected veterans with honorable/general under honorable discharge
description: Eligible Texas-connected veterans can receive up to 150 credit hours of tuition and certain fee exemptions at Texas public colleges.
caveats: Texas connection at service entry; 181 active-duty days excluding training; current Texas residence and federal tuition-benefit coordination apply. School decides; current Texas domicile alone may not establish entry connection.

title: Maryland disabled-veteran property-tax exemption
eligibility: Qualifying owner-occupants with 100% VA permanent total service-connected disability or qualifying permanent unemployability
description: Potential exemption on principal dwelling and qualifying surrounding property.
caveats: Maryland driver’s license alone does not establish entitlement. 10% or 30% alone insufficient; final rating packet and ownership/residency proof required.

title: Maryland military retirement income subtraction
eligibility: Eligible recipients of military retirement income filing Maryland taxes
description: Potential Maryland subtraction for part of qualifying military retirement income.
caveats: Filing status, age, tax-year rules and residency matter. Texas domicile and Maryland driver’s license do not by themselves establish Maryland tax liability.

title: All-state and territory veterans agencies
eligibility: Veterans seeking state-specific benefits
description: Official directory for local tax, tuition, employment, license, recreation and assistance programs.
caveats: Directory gateway, not a verified catalog of every state benefit. Residency, property location and rating thresholds vary.

title: NASDVA state benefits directory
eligibility: Veterans seeking state agency resources
description: Direct state/territory agency links and federal resources.
caveats: State agencies maintain individual benefit rules; verify specific program eligibility.

title: Military Tuition Assistance
eligibility: Eligible active-duty service members
description: Branch-funded assistance for voluntary off-duty education; generally up to $250 per semester credit hour.
geographic_scope: United States / approved overseas and online programs
caveats: Branch-specific annual limits, approvals, academic and service-obligation rules apply; request approval before enrollment.

title: DANTES-funded CLEP exams
eligibility: Eligible actively serving military, Guard and Reserve with required ID
description: First-attempt CLEP exam funding to earn college credit for prior knowledge.
geographic_scope: United States / overseas test centers and remote options
caveats: College decides credit acceptance. Retirees/separated veterans generally not DANTES-funded; some test centers charge administration fees.

title: DANTES-funded DSST exams
eligibility: Eligible actively serving military, Guard and Reserve with CAC
description: First-attempt DSST exam funding for college credit.
caveats: Retests self-funded; college decides credit. Administration fees depend on test center. Retirees and separated veterans excluded from ordinary DANTES funding.

title: VA Work Study
eligibility: Students using approved VA education benefits enrolled at least 75%
description: Paid part-time work at approved veteran-related sites while attending school.
caveats: Approved contract/site required; benefit eligibility must continue. Hours and wages follow VA rules; not automatic employment.

title: Tillman Scholars
eligibility: Military veterans, active duty and eligible spouses pursuing full-time bachelor’s, graduate or professional study
description: Competitive need-based scholarship plus leadership and career support.
caveats: 2026 class applications closed. Provider lists December 1 annual opening; check upcoming cycle. No associate degrees/certificates; US-based accredited institution required.

title: SVA John Edelman Scholarship
eligibility: Qualifying student veterans pursuing mental-health counseling careers
description: Competitive scholarship for student veterans preparing mental-health careers.
caveats: 2026 application window March 31–May 1 has closed; monitor future cycle and detailed degree requirements.

title: SVA RTX Patriot Scholarship
eligibility: Qualifying US Army student veterans
description: Competitive scholarship for Army student veterans demonstrating leadership and community engagement.
caveats: 2026 window closed; Army-specific, degree and other detailed application criteria apply.

title: Amtrak military and veteran discount
eligibility: US active military, veterans and eligible dependents/spouses
description: 10% discount on qualifying regular rail fares.
caveats: Coach restrictions, proof and fare exclusions apply; not combinable with other discounts; some services/Canadian segments excluded.

title: Apple Veterans and Military Purchase Program
eligibility: Current and veteran US military, Guard/Reserve and eligible household family
description: 10% discount through Apple’s verified military store.
caveats: ID.me verification and product/quantity/payment terms apply. Not every Apple offer or installment plan combines.

title: Under Armour military discount
eligibility: Active duty, retirees, veterans and eligible military families
description: 20% on qualifying UA.com/app/Brand House purchases; Factory House policy lists 10%.
caveats: ID.me verification. Gift cards and combining with promotional codes/sitewide promotions excluded; current terms govern.

title: Nike military discount
eligibility: Verified eligible US military customers
description: 10% single-use promotional discount on eligible products.
caveats: Member login and verification; first $500 of eligible purchase; exclusions apply. New code generally every seven days; issued code expires in two weeks.

title: Microsoft Store military discount
eligibility: Active, former and retired military personnel and families
description: Up to 10% off select Microsoft Store products.
caveats: Eligible products only; better sale price may replace discount. Does not establish a blanket software or Microsoft 365 subscription discount.

title: Verizon military and veteran mobile discount
eligibility: US active duty, retirees, veterans, eligible Guard/Reserve and certain survivors
description: Recurring discount on qualifying mobile plans after verification.
caveats: Plan/line and account rules determine amount. Cannot combine with some other occupational/student discounts; begins after verification.

title: Military TSA PreCheck access
eligibility: Eligible uniformed service members including active duty, Guard and Reserve
description: Use DoD ID as Known Traveler Number for eligible TSA PreCheck screening.
caveats: Benefit ends when military eligibility ends; retirees/veterans generally enroll separately. Boarding pass must show PreCheck. Check current TSA military enrollment instructions.

title: TSA PreCheck military-spouse enrollment discount
eligibility: Spouses with valid USID showing Spouse and Active Duty/Reserve/Guard sponsor
description: IDEMIA offers $25 off qualifying PreCheck enrollment or renewal.
caveats: Valid qualifying USID required; enrollment-vendor procedures apply. Not free automatic PreCheck and not a retiree-spouse entitlement.

title: DFW Airport military parking fee waiver
eligibility: Qualifying DV plates from any US state or listed Texas military award plates
description: Eligible vehicles can park without the normal airport parking charge.
caveats: Mounted plates and vehicle required. Valet excluded; 90 consecutive day maximum. Disable DFW TollTag use 48 hours before travel, pull entry ticket, validate via exit intercom. Accessible spaces require ISA.

title: Texas accessible parking meter fee exemption
eligibility: Valid disability placard or plate with International Symbol of Access
description: Government meter fee exemption with qualifying disability credentials.
caveats: Time limits apply unless local ordinance extends them. DV plate without ISA does not permit accessible-space parking. Mobility criteria apply separately from VA percentage; check local rules.

title: TxDOT veteran toll waiver
eligibility: Qualifying Texas specialty plates on registered vehicle
description: Toll waiver on the specific participating TxDOT roads.
caveats: Other operators have separate rules; not a statewide toll waiver. Check route and enrollment before driving. DV plate generally requires VA 50% or 40% for lower-extremity amputation.

title: Texas disabled-veteran hunting and fishing package
eligibility: VA-compensated veteran with 50%+ disability or qualifying loss of use of foot/leg
description: Free Super Combo package for eligible residents and nonresidents.
caveats: Current proof required in person. Federal duck stamp excluded. Hunting education and seasons apply. VA 10% or 30% alone insufficient.

title: Texas active-duty hunting and fishing package
eligibility: Qualifying Texas resident on full-time active military service
description: Free resident active-military Super Combo package.
caveats: Show required military records for qualifying home of record or duty station. Federal duck stamp and hunting rules still apply.

title: National parks Access Pass
eligibility: US citizen/resident with qualifying documented permanent disability
description: Free lifetime recreation pass and some amenity discounts.
caveats: Disability must substantially limit major life activities; no 100% VA requirement. Site-specific discounts and processing/shipping charges may apply.

title: Disabled Military Veteran Appreciation fishing license
eligibility: Alabama resident veteran with VA-certified disability of at least 20%.
description: Reduced-fee annual freshwater or saltwater fishing licenses.
caveats: VA letter required; 10% alone is insufficient. Separate license and endorsement rules apply.

title: Disabled veteran permanent hunting, fishing and trapping card
eligibility: Alaska resident certified at least 50% disabled; physically present in Alaska to apply.
description: Complimentary permanent identification card for hunting, sport fishing and trapping; king salmon and state waterfowl stamps waived.
caveats: Must maintain qualifying Alaska residency; harvest record and other species rules still apply.

title: Disabled veteran hunting and fishing combination license
eligibility: Arizona resident for at least one year with permanent and total 100% service-connected disability.
description: Free paper combination hunting and fishing license.
caveats: 100% individual unemployability alone is not qualifying for this license; proof and renewal conditions apply.

title: Disabled military veteran lifetime combination license
eligibility: One-year Arkansas resident with 70%+ service-connected disability, or 50%+ and a Purple Heart.
description: $52.50 lifetime hunting/fishing combination with trout and state duck stamp privileges.
caveats: VA certification required; federal duck stamp and other applicable regulations remain.

title: Reduced-fee disabled veteran sport fishing license
eligibility: Resident or nonresident honorably discharged veteran with at least 50% service-connected disability.
description: Discounted 365-day sport fishing license after CDFW prequalification.
caveats: Additional validations or species report cards may be required; not available solely for 10% or 30% ratings.

title: Veteran lifetime small game and fishing combination
eligibility: Colorado resident veteran with 50%+ combined VA service-connected rating or a Purple Heart.
description: Free lifetime small game hunting and fishing combination license; habitat stamp exemption.
caveats: Maintain Colorado residency; hunter education is required for hunting privileges. Older materials saying 60% are outdated.

title: Resident-rate outdoor licenses for active military
eligibility: Active full-time member of the U.S. armed forces.
description: Purchase Connecticut hunting, fishing or trapping licenses at resident fees.
caveats: Carry proof of full-time membership; issued through DEEP or town clerks; other permit requirements apply.

title: Resident-rate licenses for stationed active military
eligibility: Active-duty personnel stationed in Delaware.
description: Purchase recreational licenses at the Delaware resident price.
caveats: Apply through designated base recreation office or DNREC; application requires qualifying station/duty certification.

title: Military Gold Sportsman's License
eligibility: Active military stationed in Florida or Florida-resident active/retired military with qualifying ID.
description: $20 annual license bundles hunting, fresh/saltwater fishing and many state permits.
caveats: Family members do not qualify solely as dependents; excludes federal duck stamp, tarpon tags, alligator trapping and limited-entry permits.

title: One-time veterans hunting and fishing license
eligibility: Georgia-resident veteran with 90+ days active federal duty and honorable discharge on or after July 1, 2005.
description: One free year of full-privilege recreational hunting and fishing, issued once.
caveats: Hunter education and annual no-cost records may apply; federal duck stamp and commercial licenses excluded.

title: Resident hunting license rate for stationed military
eligibility: Active-duty military and dependents stationed in Hawaii.
description: Resident hunting-license price instead of the nonresident rate.
caveats: Hunter education, conservation stamp, tags and island-specific rules still apply.

title: Disabled veteran reduced license and tag fees
eligibility: Resident or nonresident veteran with VA letter confirming at least 40% service-connected disability.
description: Reduced license fees and discounted deer, elk, bear and turkey tags; resident DAV license listed at $5.
caveats: Nonresident discount tags have quotas; nonresident license and prices differ; permits cost extra.

title: Free disabled veteran hunting and fishing licenses
eligibility: Veteran receiving 10%+ service-connected compensation or total disability pension.
description: Free hunting and fishing license privilege through an IDVA disability affidavit.
caveats: Contact an IDVA Veteran Service Office for privilege card; stamps, species permits and other rules may remain.

title: Disabled American Veteran hunting and fishing license
eligibility: Indiana resident with military service and documented service-connected disability.
description: $2.75 annual small-game hunting and fishing license; $27.50 ten-year option.
caveats: DNR approval and documentation required; deer, turkey and stamps excluded. Page does not specify a minimum percentage.

title: Disabled veteran lifetime hunting and fishing
eligibility: Iowa resident for at least 90 days, active federal service other than training, entitled to service-connected rating; qualifying DD214.
description: Lifetime hunting and/or fishing license listed at $7 including administration.
caveats: Application asks for honorable or general under honorable conditions DD214; hunter education and annual fish/wildlife fees still apply.

title: Disabled veteran free permanent hunting and fishing licenses
eligibility: Kansas resident with qualifying discharge and service-connected disability of at least 30%.
description: Free permanent hunting and fishing licenses under KSA 32-934.
caveats: Program page says honorably discharged; state veterans guide also lists general under honorable conditions. Confirm discharge documentation with KDWP; hunter education may apply.

title: Disabled Sportsman's License
eligibility: Kentucky resident veteran at least 50% disabled due to service-connected disability.
description: Special license includes combination hunting/fishing, deer, turkey, trout and state migratory bird/waterfowl permits.
caveats: Disability authorization required and expires after three years; annual license purchase, HIP survey and federal duck stamp still apply.

title: Disabled veteran driver's license fee exemption
eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with 50%+ service-related disability receiving federal disability compensation, meeting statutory registration exclusion.
description: Exemption from specified Louisiana driver's license or special identification-card issuance fees.
caveats: Statute excludes persons subject to specified sex-offender registration requirements and preserves fee under RS 32:668(B)(1)(a)(i); proof required.

title: Disabled veteran complimentary hunting and fishing
eligibility: Honorably discharged veteran with 50%+ service-connected disability residing in Maine or qualifying reciprocal state.
description: Complimentary lifetime hunting/fishing/trapping license with listed endorsements.
caveats: Residency and reciprocity must continue; lottery applications still required. Verify home-state reciprocity with Maine.

title: Complimentary POW-DAV lifetime hunting license
eligibility: Maryland resident with 100% service-connected disability, VA unemployability determination or former POW status.
description: Complimentary lifetime hunting license including bow, muzzleloader, sika deer and furbearer privileges.
caveats: VA certification and application required; annual migratory bird stamps, federal duck stamp and harvest record remain where applicable.

title: Local disabled veteran property-tax exemption
eligibility: Qualifying Massachusetts resident veteran with 10%+ service-connected disability, domicile and residency-history requirements.
description: Base $400 local property-tax exemption tier; municipality may offer enhanced amount.
caveats: Municipal adoption and local amount matter; occupy domicile July 1 and meet six-month pre-service or five-year residency route. Confirm with assessor.

title: Free hunting licenses for disabled veterans
eligibility: Michigan resident VA-rated permanently/totally disabled at 100% benefit rate, other than blindness, or individually unemployable.
description: Free hunting licenses that do not require a separate application.
caveats: Carry VA proof when obtaining and using license; drawn/application licenses excluded; 10% alone does not qualify.

title: Free annual state park vehicle permit
eligibility: Minnesota resident veteran with any level of service-related disability.
description: Free annual state park vehicle permit.
caveats: Bring qualifying disability/veteran documentation; vehicle entrance permit does not itself waive camping charges.

title: Disabled resident hunting and fishing license exemption
eligibility: Mississippi resident with VA-certified 100% service-connected disability, or another listed qualifying disability.
description: Exemption from purchasing hunting and fishing licenses.
caveats: Carry proof of residency and disability unless optional exempt license purchased; check separate saltwater, stamp and activity rules.

title: Disabled veteran hunting permit exemption
eligibility: Honorably discharged resident or nonresident veteran with 60%+ service-related disability or former POW; qualifying military medical patients also eligible.
description: Hunt qualifying wildlife without standard permit and receive resident permit prices where specified.
caveats: Carry certified VA eligibility or assignment orders; black bear, deer, elk, turkey, trapping, migratory bird and federal duck stamp exceptions apply.

title: Disabled Veteran Assistance Program
eligibility: 100% service-connected disability; own and occupy primary home at least seven months; annual income limits.
description: Reduces the home property-tax rate by 50%, 70%, 80%, or 100% according to income and marital status.
caveats: 10% or a prospective 30% medical retirement alone does not qualify. Income limits change by tax year; apply by April 15.

title: Veteran homestead exemption
eligibility: Qualifying homeowners including veterans totally disabled by service-connected injury or illness and certain VA-adapted-home recipients.
description: Property-tax relief through Nebraska homestead exemption categories.
caveats: 10% alone is not the totally disabled category. Category-specific disability, income and home-value rules require county assessor review.

title: Veteran property or vehicle tax exemption
eligibility: Nevada resident with qualifying 90-day active service and honorable discharge/satisfactory service, or still serving; disabled tier requires permanent service-connected disability and honorable discharge.
description: Apply an annual exemption to assessed property value or vehicle Governmental Services Tax; disability tiers begin at 60%.
caveats: Not a blanket vehicle registration waiver. Dollar amounts are inflation adjusted; use only one exemption and one county.

title: Veterans property-tax credit
eligibility: At least 90 days of active service in a qualifying war/conflict; continuing service or honorable discharge/separation; residency and property rules.
description: A $50 standard annual residential property-tax credit, with a locally adopted amount from $51 to $750.
caveats: Local amount varies. Separate all-veterans credit requires municipal adoption; consult assessor for residency and filing.

title: $250 veteran property-tax deduction
eligibility: New Jersey legal resident and property owner with qualifying active-duty service and honorable discharge.
description: Deduct $250 annually from qualifying property taxes.
caveats: Requirements generally must be met October 1 of preceding year. Active duty for training does not qualify.

title: Reduced-fee small-game and fishing license
eligibility: New Mexico service-connected disabled veterans; proof of disability.
description: A $10 small-game and fishing license is available regardless of service-connected disability percentage.
caveats: This is not an all-species or big-game license. Free lifetime license separately requires 100% service-connected disability.

title: Alternative veterans property-tax exemption
eligibility: Qualifying wartime/expeditionary service, primary residence and eligible ownership; discharge under honorable conditions or approved Restoration of Honor determination. Certain career active members with ten years qualify.
description: Reduces assessed residential value; qualifying disability can increase the exemption.
caveats: Local adoption and caps govern savings. Active service eligibility requires the detailed reenlistment/service tests; no universal dishonorable-discharge eligibility.

title: Disabled veteran homestead exclusion
eligibility: Honorable/under honorable conditions separation and permanent total service-connected disability or qualifying specially adapted housing benefits.
description: Excludes the first $45,000 of assessed primary-residence value for qualifying veterans or surviving spouses.
caveats: 10% alone does not qualify. Certification and county application required; no age or income limit.

title: Disabled Veteran property-tax credit
eligibility: Veterans with service-connected disability of at least 50%; qualifying owned and occupied homestead.
description: Reduces taxable homestead value; a qualifying move can transfer credit to the new homestead.
caveats: A 10% or 30% rating alone does not reach this threshold. Ask county about documentation and deadlines.

title: Enhanced disabled veteran homestead exemption
eligibility: Qualifying primary-home owner with 100% service-connected disability or total disability compensation based on individual unemployability.
description: Property-tax reduction under the enhanced veteran homestead category.
caveats: 10% alone does not qualify. Current application explicitly includes individual unemployability; annual exemption value is inflation adjusted.

title: Disabled veteran sales-tax exemption
eligibility: Oklahoma resident with permanent disability receiving service-connected compensation at the 100% rate, certified by VA.
description: Sales-tax exemption permit covering up to $25,000 of qualifying purchases annually.
caveats: Not $25,000 cash. 10% alone does not qualify. New applicants also need Oklahoma Veterans Registry verification.

title: Disabled veteran homestead exemption
eligibility: Oregon resident, own and live in home, qualifying veteran with disability of at least 40%; honorable service documentation.
description: Exempts part of homestead assessed value; larger exemption for qualifying service-connected disabilities.
caveats: 10%/30% alone do not reach 40%. Physician-certified route has additional requirements; generally file by April 1.

title: Disabled veteran real-estate tax exemption
eligibility: State resident; honorable/under honorable conditions discharge; qualifying wartime service; principal owned dwelling; qualifying permanent 100%, TDIU, or listed severe service-connected losses; financial need.
description: Exempts eligible principal residence from real-estate taxes after state approval.
caveats: Not automatic at 10% or 30%. Income above presumptive level may still qualify if verified allowable expenses exceed income.

title: Disabled Veterans Tuition Waiver
eligibility: Permanent Rhode Island resident veteran with 10–100% service-connected disability; apply for and use financial aid first.
description: Tuition waiver at Rhode Island public colleges and universities.
caveats: Other fees and charges are excluded. Academic admission requirements still apply.

title: Disabled veteran vehicle property-tax exemption
eligibility: Veteran totally and permanently disabled from a service-connected disability.
description: Property-tax exemption for two qualifying private passenger vehicles owned or leased.
caveats: 10% or 30% alone does not meet total-and-permanent requirement; submit state exemption application.

title: Disabled veteran owner-occupied dwelling exemption
eligibility: Veteran rated permanently and totally disabled from service-connected disability; own and occupy qualifying dwelling.
description: Exempts $200,000 of qualifying dwelling value from property taxation.
caveats: 10%/30% alone do not qualify. Surviving-spouse categories have their own amounts and requirements.

title: Disabled veteran property-tax relief
eligibility: Own primary residence; service-connected permanent total disability or specified severe service-connected losses, or qualifying POW disability.
description: State reimbursement of part or all of qualifying paid property taxes, calculated on value up to the program cap.
caveats: 10%/30% alone do not qualify. Apply through county trustee; state page lists $175,000 maximum market value for calculation.

title: Partial disabled veteran property exemption
eligibility: Texas resident with certified service-related disability of at least 10%; one designated owned property.
caveats: These amounts reduce taxable property value, not the tax bill dollar-for-dollar. Separate 100%/IU homestead exemption has different rules.

title: Disabled veteran property-tax abatement
eligibility: Qualifying permanent residence and military service-connected disability rating of at least 10%.
description: Reduces taxable property value using disability percentage multiplied by the state maximum abatement base.
caveats: Base changes over time. Submit VA benefits letter and county application by September 1; refiling required for specified changes.

title: Veteran property-tax exemption
eligibility: Eligible primary-home owner receiving VA disability compensation at 50%+, qualifying pension, or permanent medical military retirement pay.
description: Reduces appraised residence value by $10,000 minimum, with town option up to $40,000.
caveats: Medical retirement is an alternative eligibility route, not proof of a 50% VA rating. Generally verify by May 1; 2026 application period closed.

title: Disabled veteran real-property tax exemption
eligibility: Veteran with VA 100% service-connected permanent and total disability; qualifying owned principal residence.
description: Exempts principal residence and up to one acre from real-property tax.
caveats: 10% or medical retirement at 30% alone does not qualify. Apply with local commissioner of revenue; qualifying surviving spouses have separate conditions.

title: Lifetime Disabled Veteran park pass
eligibility: Washington resident veteran with combined service-connected disability of at least 30%; residency and VA award evidence.
description: Free day-use parking, camping/moorage, boat launch and trailer dump at qualifying state parks; accepted at Discover Pass lands.
caveats: VA service-connected rating required; a DoD retirement rating alone is insufficient evidence. Cabins, yurts, extra-vehicle fees and Sno-Parks excluded; stay limits apply.

title: Military and disabled veteran hunting/fishing privileges
eligibility: Resident veterans qualifying for VA auto grant, VA 100% permanent total disability, or former POW status; active duty on leave/furlough have separate privilege.
description: Qualifying veterans may obtain free hunting, trapping and fishing licenses; active-duty leave papers can substitute for licenses.
caveats: 10% alone is not the disabled-veteran threshold. Follow hunting seasons and other wildlife rules; carry required status documentation.

title: Veterans property-tax credit
eligibility: Wisconsin resident veteran with honorable active service, 100% service-connected rating or individual unemployability; entered service as resident or five consecutive years residency afterward.
description: Refundable state tax credit for qualifying paid property taxes on primary residence and up to one acre.
caveats: WDVA certification required. 10%/30% alone do not qualify. Joint ownership and business portions limit claim.

title: Veteran property or vehicle tax exemption
eligibility: Current Wyoming resident with three years in state; qualifying honorably discharged wartime/campaign veteran, certain disabled veteran, or eligible surviving spouse.
description: Exempts $6,000 of assessed value; may be applied to primary residence property tax or motor-vehicle registration.
caveats: Not a $6,000 cash payment. Apply by fourth Monday in May for property relief; assessor must verify service/disability category.

title: Army Recovery Care adaptive reconditioning
description: Modified exercise, sports and therapeutic activities support recovery from injury or illness.
eligibility: Eligible Soldiers assigned to a Soldier Recovery Unit and cleared by its physical therapist.
caveats: Participation follows your medical profile and recovery plan; RM2 Soldiers are excluded on the published program page.
next_step: Ask your SRU physical therapist about activities that fit your profile.

title: Move United Warfighters
description: Free adaptive sports help you try activities such as skiing, cycling and paddling with adapted equipment.
eligibility: Service members and veterans with a permanent physical disability; combat and noncombat injuries from any era.
caveats: Military-specific events are free; confirm each event’s travel arrangements and available adaptations.
next_step: Submit the Warfighters interest form to find nearby programs.

title: VA national adaptive sports and arts events
description: Find VA rehabilitation events ranging from winter sports and golf to wheelchair competition and creative arts.
eligibility: Veterans who meet the chosen event’s medical and VA-care criteria.
caveats: This is an event directory; each event has separate eligibility, referral, registration and travel rules. VA grants fund organizations rather than giving every participant a cash grant.
next_step: Ask VA recreation therapy which event fits your interests.

title: National Veterans Wheelchair Games
description: Try wheelchair sports and compete alongside other veterans with mobility disabilities.
eligibility: Veterans eligible for care at a VA medical facility who meet the Games’ medical criteria.
caveats: Registration requires medical review; a VA percentage alone does not establish eligibility. Annual dates and application windows change.
source_type: VA / Paralyzed Veterans of America event
next_step: Review medical criteria with your VA clinician.

title: National Veterans Summer Sports Clinic
description: An immersive rehabilitation experience uses fitness, sports and teamwork to support a healthier routine at home.
eligibility: Published 2027 criteria: veterans age 55 or younger actively seen in VA mental health programs, referred by their VA mental health provider.
caveats: These are current event-specific criteria, not a blanket benefit for all disabled veterans. Ask the referring team about costs and travel.
next_step: Ask your VA mental health provider about referral.

title: Warrior Sailing basic training
description: A three-day sailing camp teaches boating and teamwork to wounded, ill or injured military participants.
eligibility: Wounded, ill or injured service members and veterans from all U.S. military branches.
caveats: Camp instruction, equipment, meals and local transport are covered. Participants outside the local region pay travel to the camp; selection and dates vary.
next_step: Check upcoming camps and ask about your functional needs.

title: Project Healing Waters
description: Learn fly fishing, casting, fly tying and rod building, then join fishing outings. Equipment and participant trips are free.
eligibility: Injured or ill service members need a qualifying in-line-of-duty condition and provider recommendation. Veterans qualify through a VA disability rating, authorized VA referral, or an interim military disability rating pending VA determination.
caveats: Join the local program before requesting trips; the group verifies its participation requirements.
geographic_scope: United States; local programs, including Texas and Maryland
next_step: Contact the nearest program lead.

title: Texas Parasport military connections
description: Find adaptive sports, equipment connections and support close to home in Texas.
eligibility: Wounded, ill or injured military community members; individual partner programs set participation rules.
caveats: This is a connection service and program network; costs and eligibility differ by sport and provider.
next_step: Contact Texas Parasport with your location and preferred activities.

title: K9s For Warriors service dogs
description: Trained dogs perform disability-related tasks to help veterans with service-connected PTSD, traumatic brain injury, or military sexual trauma.
eligibility: Veterans of any era with the provider’s verified qualifying clinical diagnosis and application approval.
caveats: Dog and residential training are free; participant travel is not included. Waitlist and screening apply; they do not train your own pet. Currently serving applicants should use the prescreener rather than assume eligibility.
geographic_scope: All 50 states, Puerto Rico and Guam; travel to training required
next_step: Complete the program prescreener and discuss documentation with your clinician.

title: America’s VetDogs
description: Guide, hearing and service dogs can assist with practical tasks or qualifying PTSD-related needs.
eligibility: Active military and honorably discharged veterans with qualifying disabilities. Published PTSD criteria specify combat-related PTSD and at least one year of consistent mental health care.
caveats: Dog, training, campus accommodation and transportation are free. Two-week residential training and ongoing dog-care responsibilities apply; waitlist varies. Ask admissions about the separate MST program.
geographic_scope: United States; training in New York; residency exceptions case by case
next_step: Request the admissions application for the appropriate dog program.

title: Canine Companions veterans service dogs
description: Free service dogs help with physical tasks, hearing needs or service-connected PTSD.
eligibility: U.S. veterans with qualifying physical disability, hearing loss or service-connected PTSD, subject to provider assessment.
caveats: Application and matching are required; verify current training location, travel costs and wait time. These are task-trained service dogs.
geographic_scope: United States; regional centers, including Texas
next_step: Contact the Veterans Program Manager or start the applicant questionnaire.

title: Warrior Canine Connection service dogs
description: Free trained dogs help with mobility limitations, PTSD, or traumatic brain injury.
eligibility: Veterans or members in later medical-separation evaluation stages, with qualifying disability, provider support and treatment participation.
caveats: Waits can be long. At least eight days of Maryland team training; travel and lodging generally your responsibility. No pet-dog training.
geographic_scope: Maryland training; contact provider about placement geography
next_step: Email Client Services to discuss medical-transition timing.

title: Patriot PAWS service dogs
description: Free service dogs help disabled veterans with mobility limitations or post-traumatic stress.
eligibility: Honorably discharged veterans may apply; each application receives individual review and a background check.
caveats: Provider estimates 12–24 months to match. Confirm travel and training logistics. In-home working dogs are a separate option with different access limits.
geographic_scope: Texas-based; ask coordinator about nationwide placement
next_step: Apply through the Service Dog application and speak with the Veteran Coordinator.

title: VA service-dog veterinary benefit
description: VA may cover veterinary care and necessary equipment for an approved guide, hearing or mobility service dog.
eligibility: Veterans prescribed a qualifying dog for visual, hearing or substantial mobility impairment; VA clinical approval and ADI/IGDF-accredited team training required.
caveats: VA does not supply dogs universally. PTSD alone is not a qualifying impairment under this published insurance benefit; routine food, grooming and boarding are not generally covered.
geographic_scope: United States; contact VA about coverage geography
next_step: Request evaluation through your VA provider and Prosthetics service.

title: Warrior Canine Connection family support dogs
description: An in-home companion can support relationships and daily family life.
eligibility: Active-duty members, veterans or Gold Star families with provider support and a suitable household.
caveats: This family-support dog has no service-dog public-access rights. Training and travel requirements apply; dog and training have no fee.
geographic_scope: Maryland training; ask about placement geography
next_step: Ask Client Services whether the family-support placement fits your household.

title: Operation Kindness military pet-adoption discount
description: Save 25% on adoption fees for a companion pet.
eligibility: Veterans and active military with valid military ID under the published year-round offer.
caveats: This is pet adoption, not a trained service-dog program. Confirm the discount and accepted proof before visiting.
next_step: Bring military ID and ask the adoption team about the discount.

title: Team Red, White & Blue chapters
description: Meet other veterans and service members through local exercise and social activities.
eligibility: Veterans, active-duty members, Guard, Reserve and civilian supporters.
caveats: Activities and schedules vary by chapter; check the event listing for any costs or accessibility needs.
geographic_scope: United States and listed overseas chapters
next_step: Find your chapter and browse events in the member app.

title: Team Rubicon volunteering
description: Use your skills for disaster relief, local service projects or remote volunteer work while meeting a service-minded community.
eligibility: Veterans, active-duty members and civilians can join.
caveats: Field deployment requires profile completion, TR101 and a background check; each role has suitability requirements. This is volunteering, not a cash benefit or employment.
geographic_scope: United States; remote roles and selected international operations
next_step: Register as a Greyshirt and choose roles that fit your abilities.

title: The Mission Continues service platoons
description: Join veterans and neighbors for community projects and social events.
eligibility: Everyone is welcome, regardless of veteran status.
caveats: Local projects and accessibility vary. The program is now part of Travis Manion Foundation following its 2025 acquisition.
next_step: Find a nearby platoon and sign up for a suitable project.

title: Texas Military Veteran Peer Network
description: Connect with trained military and veteran peers for local support, networking and referrals.
eligibility: Texas military and veteran community; local teams can explain access for family members and service status.
caveats: Peer support is not a substitute for clinical treatment. Services and meeting formats vary by county.
next_step: Use TexVet’s county filter to contact your local peer coordinator.

title: Maryland’s Commitment to Veterans
description: Care coordinators and peers help connect you with health and community resources.
eligibility: U.S. uniformed service members, veterans and their families in Maryland.
caveats: This is coordination and referral support; the receiving program determines its own eligibility and costs.
next_step: Contact the regional resource coordinator.

title: Warrior Canine Connection dog-training recovery
description: Help train a future service dog for another veteran while practicing communication and emotional-regulation skills.
eligibility: Recovering warriors; provider states participation is available through referral or self-enrollment, regardless of branch or discharge status.
caveats: Therapeutic dog-training participation does not mean you receive a dog; ask about location and intake availability.
next_step: Ask about Mission Based Trauma Recovery sessions near you.

title: Wounded Warrior Project community and wellness
description: Free connection events and wellness, benefits and transition support help you find useful services and community.
eligibility: Post-9/11 service members in good standing and honorably discharged veterans; other discharges reviewed case by case. Physical or combat injury is not required by the current registration FAQ.
caveats: Registration verification applies; individual programs can add clinical criteria. In-person and virtual options vary.
next_step: Register or ask the Resource Center which programs fit your needs.

title: Wounded Warrior Project Landstuhl support
description: A WWP team offers comfort items and connections to recovery resources after medical evacuation.
eligibility: Post-9/11 service members medically evacuated from deployed locations to Landstuhl Regional Medical Center.
caveats: This specific overseas service is tied to medical evacuation; it is not a universal overseas grant.
next_step: Ask the Landstuhl care team about WWP support.

title: Vet Center counseling
description: Community-based individual, group and family counseling can help with military trauma and readjustment.
eligibility: Veterans and current service members meeting an eligibility route such as combat or hostility service, military sexual trauma, qualifying disaster response or certain education-related readjustment needs.
caveats: Eligibility is event- and service-based; VA enrollment and a disability rating are not required. Counseling is free, but ask the center which eligibility route applies.
next_step: Contact a Vet Center for an eligibility conversation.

title: VA PTSD Coach and National Center for PTSD
description: Free information and self-help tools explain trauma symptoms, coping skills and evidence-based treatments.
eligibility: Public resources and the PTSD Coach app are available to anyone.
caveats: The app cannot diagnose PTSD or replace professional evaluation or treatment.
next_step: Explore Learn and Manage Symptoms, then discuss treatment options with a clinician.

title: Warrior Care Network
description: An intensive treatment program helps with service-related PTSD, military sexual trauma, traumatic brain injury, and related symptoms.
eligibility: Service members and veterans who served on or after September 11, 2001, have qualifying service-related symptoms and can attend for at least two weeks; diagnosis is not required to apply.
caveats: Clinical screening applies; not intended for someone currently in crisis. No participant cost; insurance may be billed.
geographic_scope: United States; participating academic medical centers
next_step: Ask WWP’s Resource Center for a clinical-program screening.

title: The Headstrong Project trauma therapy
description: Get matched with a trauma therapist for up to 30 fully covered eligible sessions without using insurance.
eligibility: Veterans of any era, Guard, Reserve, and transitioning members within three months of separation or retirement; location and clinical review apply.
caveats: The 30 sessions are a lifetime program benefit; later sessions require a copayment. State licensing, availability and funding limit access. Privacy has legal safety exceptions.
geographic_scope: Participating U.S. states; in-person and telehealth
next_step: Check service areas and complete Connect to Care.

title: Cohen Veterans Network clinics
description: Mental health clinics offer therapy for PTSD, depression, anxiety and family concerns.
eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans, active-duty members with a TRICARE referral, Guard, Reserve and military families; veterans served regardless of discharge status.
caveats: Insurance and payment arrangements vary; no-insurance care may be free and the provider says cost should not block access. Confirm local clinic coverage.
geographic_scope: Participating U.S. clinic regions; verify current overseas locations
next_step: Find a clinic and ask about eligibility, telehealth and costs.

title: Stop Soldier Suicide ROGER care
description: Free personalized virtual care focuses on safety planning, suicide prevention and support for life stressors.
eligibility: U.S. service members and veterans of any era or discharge status.
caveats: Independent of DoD and VA; confirm clinical availability and privacy exceptions with the intake team. It does not provide grants or direct financial assistance.
geographic_scope: Virtual; ask about care where you are physically located
next_step: Use the provider’s care-request form to discuss support.

title: Military mental health evaluation access: Brandon Act
description: Request a mental health evaluation directly through a military clinic or with help from your leadership.
eligibility: Currently serving service members covered by their service’s implementation, including Army Soldiers.
caveats: Medical confidentiality has legal and safety limits; it is not an unconditional guarantee against command notification. Appointment and referral procedures depend on location.
next_step: Contact your military behavioral health clinic or request a referral from your supervisor.

title: Army chaplain confidential support
description: Talk with a chaplain about personal stress, grief, relationships or spiritual concerns.
eligibility: Army service members and military families; contact the installation for other eligible populations.
caveats: Privilege applies to private communications made to a chaplain as a spiritual adviser or matter of conscience. Chaplain support is different from clinical treatment.
next_step: Contact your unit or installation chaplain and ask for a private conversation.

title: Walt Disney World Military Salute tickets · 2026
description: Discounted multi-day Disney World tickets for eligible military members and their families. This is a paid ticket offer.
eligibility: Active duty and military retirees, eligible Guard/Reserve and qualifying spouses with valid military ID
caveats: Valid through December 18, 2026; November 22–28 blocked. Park reservations and sponsor activation required; six-ticket limit with sponsor-use rules. Parking and other extras excluded. Ordinary veteran status or VA 10% alone is not the listed qualification.
next_step: Ask your Army MWR ticket office about the appropriate ticket and check park reservations before buying.

title: Disneyland military tickets · 2026
description: Special-price Disneyland tickets, including three- and four-day Park Hopper options.
eligibility: Eligible active-duty or retired military and qualifying spouses with current military ID
caveats: Three-/four-day tickets: purchase by December 27, use by December 31, 2026. Reservations required; up to six promotional tickets and sponsor-use requirements. One-day offer has separate dates. Check current ID and ticket rules.
next_step: Check Disneyland reservations and ask an authorized military ticket office for the current options.
verification: Military ID / ticket office or GOVX

title: Disneyland Paris military ticket discount
description: Eligible military members can get a special ticket rate for a visit to Disneyland Paris.
eligibility: Active or retired military with accepted French, UK or US government proof of service
caveats: Check the specific military product, dates, guest limits and required original ID. A veteran designation alone may not satisfy retired-military documentation. Travel and lodging cost extra.
next_step: Select the military special-rate option and review accepted proof before purchasing.

title: Atlantis Bahamas military appreciation discount
description: Verify your military status through ID.me for up to 30% off the resort’s Best Available Rates.
eligibility: Military customers who pass the offer’s ID.me verification
caveats: A percentage discount, not a free stay. Dates, room availability and final checkout terms govern; compare total including taxes, resort fees, transport and meals. Provider page does not spell out every veteran/discharge category.
next_step: Use Atlantis’s official military offer and compare the full trip price before booking.

title: Atlantis via Caesars SALUTE / Platinum · conditional nights
description: Caesars SALUTE gives eligible military customers Platinum status. Its 2026 Atlantis partner offer lists complimentary nights for selected months, with substantial conditions.
eligibility: Verified Caesars SALUTE military/veteran members with Platinum status and Atlantis offer approval
caveats: Platinum: four complimentary Coral nights in Jan/May/Jun/Sep/Oct; Feb/Aug/Nov/Dec buy two at $150 each, get two complimentary. Book and travel by Feb 1, 2027, subject to availability. Terms require four hours of rated casino play or retail package charges. Resort fees, meals, flights, VAT and gratuities are not included unless specified. Confirm SALUTE-linked eligibility and all charges directly before booking.
next_step: Verify SALUTE in person, then ask Atlantis VIP Services to confirm your specific Platinum offer, play condition, fees and cancellation terms in writing.

title: Caesars SALUTE military benefits
description: Military membership provides Platinum status plus selected hotel, dining, shopping and parking benefits.
eligibility: Active-duty, Guard/Reserve, veterans, retirees and eligible spouses with accepted proof
caveats: Verify ID in person at a Caesars Rewards Center. Destination terms vary. Atlantis is a separate conditional partner benefit; SALUTE status does not make every stay or parking location free.
next_step: Bring accepted military/veteran ID to a Caesars Rewards Center and ask about current SALUTE benefits.

title: Shades of Green military resort
description: Stay at a military recreation resort near Disney World. Room eligibility and ticket eligibility are separate questions.
eligibility: Active duty, retirees and other authorized patrons; qualifying service-connected veterans with required credentials
caveats: Paid rooms, subject to availability. Expanded veteran access uses specified VHIC or alternative documents. Disney Salute ticket requirements can be stricter than resort access. Separate January/September program for other honorably discharged veterans.
next_step: Read your eligibility category, confirm required ID and compare room rates; verify any tickets separately.

title: Universal Orlando Military Freedom Pass · 2026
description: Eligible military customers can buy a promotional pass for repeated park visits during the offer period.
eligibility: Qualifying military or DoD ID holders under Universal’s ticket rules
caveats: Use through December 18, 2026; blockouts apply. Two-/three-park options differ. Volcano Bay excluded October 26–December 18 during closure; Epic Universe is a separate add-on. Buy through authorized military offices; sponsor activation and ticket limits apply.
next_step: Ask Army MWR to verify your ID category and park choices before buying.

title: SeaWorld Waves of Honor · active duty
description: Eligible active-duty military can receive a complimentary one-day visit under the park’s military program.
eligibility: Eligible active-duty US military and qualifying guests under the selected park offer
caveats: Verify the chosen park’s ID, guest limits, redemption and expiration dates. Parking, extras and other parks are not automatically included. Veteran offers have separate seasonal windows; an expired veteran promotion is not an active entitlement.
next_step: Visit the official Waves of Honor page for your park and complete eligibility verification before travel.

title: American Forces Travel
description: A military travel site with negotiated hotel, cruise, flight, rental-car and event offers. Compare the final price with other booking options.
eligibility: Eligible MWR patrons, including active duty, retirees and qualifying veterans
caveats: Verification required. Savings vary; taxes, resort fees, cancellation restrictions and other charges can apply. Offers are paid travel unless specifically stated otherwise.
next_step: Verify eligibility through American Forces Travel and compare the total cost and cancellation terms.

title: ID.me military offer directory
description: Browse current military and veteran offers from participating brands, including travel, clothing, electronics and everyday services.
eligibility: Eligible military communities verified by ID.me; each brand sets additional rules.
caveats: Directory offers change. A verified military account does not override a merchant’s exclusions, discharge rules, location limits, fees or terms. Cash back and discounts are different benefits; compare the final price.
next_step: Choose an offer, review its terms and use the provider’s ID.me verification link.

title: Army Emergency Relief — rent, deposits and temporary lodging
description: Help with rent, initial rental deposits, utilities or temporary lodging through zero-interest loans, grants or a combination.
eligibility: Active-duty Army Soldiers; medically retired Army Soldiers including TDRL/PDRL; eligible dependents.
caveats: Individual financial-need review; a grant is not guaranteed. Medical retirement preserves eligibility; ordinary separation plus a VA rating alone does not establish retired status.
next_step: Apply online or contact your installation AER officer now; request a transition budget review and ask whether your need qualifies for a grant.
help_type: Rent / deposit / temporary lodging / loan or grant
timing: Start before separation; medically retired Soldiers can also apply afterward.

title: Operation Homefront — Transitional Housing Villages
description: Furnished rent-free apartments with utilities and internet while medically separating families establish civilian income.
eligibility: Wounded, ill or injured service members with families about to medically separate, or recently medically separated and awaiting VA compensation.
caveats: Placement and openings required. Maryland primarily serves Walter Reed/Bethesda and Fort Belvoir treatment patients; San Antonio primarily JBSA/Audie Murphy; not a portable rent payment or a Houston apartment.
geographic_scope: Gaithersburg, Maryland / San Antonio, Texas / San Diego, California
next_step: Email transitionalhousing@operationhomefront.org and apply through My Operation Homefront; describe medical separation date, family and treatment location.

title: Operation Homefront — Critical Financial Assistance (rent route)
description: Short-term help with rent or mortgage and other essential bills during a documented financial hardship.
eligibility: Post-9/11 line-of-duty wound, illness or injury; if discharged, honorable or general under honorable conditions and within 10 years. Separate qualifying deployed E1–E6 route also exists.
caveats: General active-duty E1–E6 with dependents category alone covers food and dependent vision, not rent. Amount and months depend on review; not guaranteed transition income.
next_step: Call 877-264-3968 to confirm rent-route eligibility. Gather LOD/injury records, DD214 if separated, income and rent bill, then submit during monthly window.
timing: Applications open 1st–10th monthly; process updated January 2026. Next window after October 16: November 1–10; verify deadline at https://operationhomefront.org/cfa-process/.

title: Operation Homefront — Transitional Housing Apartments
description: A selected apartment with rent, utilities and internet covered for one year plus financial and employment counseling.
eligibility: Veterans with or without family within four years of honorable or general under honorable conditions discharge; injury/combat deployment not required.
caveats: Security deposit is paid by veteran. Only Tacoma WA and Salt Lake City UT applications currently advertised as open; Frederick/Columbia MD and San Antonio TX are program locations, not confirmed current openings.
geographic_scope: Maryland / Texas / Georgia / Utah / Washington (limited openings)
next_step: Check current application status; ask about a waitlist or reopening for Maryland or Texas.
timing: 12 months; published typical application processing 30–45 days.

title: Operation Homefront — Transitional Homes for Veterans
description: Rent-free home placement while a family works toward employment, education and financial stability.
eligibility: Transitioning active duty, reservist and veteran families within ten years of discharge.
caveats: Competitive, location-specific homes and case management; cannot assume a home is available near Houston or DMV. Not cash for your current lease.
next_step: Review available homes in My Operation Homefront and ask about selection requirements and geographic fit.

title: VA SSVF — short-term rent, deposits and moving assistance
description: Local nonprofit providers may pay rent, security or utility deposits and moving costs to prevent or end veteran homelessness.
eligibility: Veteran households meeting current income and homelessness or imminent-risk screening; generally discharge other than dishonorable. Local provider verifies current rules.
caveats: Not an automatic benefit for everyone leaving military. Amount, duration and availability vary; apply before committing to costs. Provider income webpages may lag national changes; request current income/disability-income treatment.
next_step: Ask VA homeless services for the SSVF provider serving your destination ZIP and a pre-separation referral; request screening for post-discharge income and housing risk.
timing: Seek referral now; provider determines enrollment timing and eligibility after separation.

title: U.S.VETS Houston — SSVF and move-in support
description: Houston team offers rent payments, eviction prevention, move-in and utility help, housing search and case management for eligible veterans.
eligibility: Veterans/families screened for SSVF or other local housing programs, including income and homelessness-risk requirements.
caveats: Financial assistance is case-specific and funding-dependent; not a blanket three-month rent grant. Houston program fact sheet verifies services, not individual eligibility or a vacancy.
next_step: Call 832-203-1626 and request SSVF intake for your proposed Houston ZIP; disclose separation date, projected income and deposit/rent need.
timing: Ask intake about referral before discharge and available enrollment after discharge.

title: Friendship Place — Veterans First (DMV)
description: Veteran rapid-rehousing and homelessness-prevention case management helps locate housing and connect to move-in and benefits support.
eligibility: Veteran or veteran household; other than dishonorable discharge; homeless or at risk. Page lists income below 50% area median; ask intake for current screening.
caveats: County service boundaries and income/risk screening apply; no guaranteed rent award.
geographic_scope: Washington DC; Montgomery, Prince George’s and Frederick Maryland; Fairfax, Loudoun, Prince William and Arlington Virginia; Alexandria Virginia
next_step: Call 202-658-9599 or email vfscreen@friendshipplace.org for Veterans First intake.

title: Housing Counseling Services — DMV SSVF
description: Case-managed help can cover rent arrears, security deposit or first rent, utility deposits, moving and emergency housing.
eligibility: Veterans not dishonorably discharged; within service area; homeless or imminent risk; income eligibility (provider currently lists up to 80% area median).
caveats: Payments go to third parties case by case. Page contains older linked 2025 income tables; request current limits rather than assuming a quoted table applies.
geographic_scope: Washington DC; Prince George’s and Montgomery Maryland; Fairfax and Arlington Virginia; Alexandria Virginia
next_step: Call 202-667-7366 or email ssvfprogram@housingetc.org; request eligibility screening and a destination-specific rent/deposit plan.
help_type: Rent arrears / first rent / deposits / moving

title: Texas Veterans Commission — local grant-funded rent assistance
