description: Find local organizations funded to help Texas veterans with rent, deposits and other essential bills.
eligibility: Texas veterans/dependents/survivors with financial need, meeting provider service-area and program rules.
caveats: TVC grants fund organizations, not direct individual applications. Texas domicile alone does not establish local service eligibility while living elsewhere; ask provider about actual residence.
next_step: Search the TVC grant-provider directory for your Houston-area county and financial assistance; apply to the listed organization.

title: Maryland Veterans Trust Fund — overdue housing bills
description: One-time grant paid to vendors can help clear overdue rent, mortgage or utilities during a temporary hardship.
eligibility: Maryland residents who are honorably discharged veterans; Maryland National Guard members; qualifying surviving spouses.
caveats: Requires Maryland residency, not merely a Maryland driver’s license. Bills must be at least 30–60 days overdue under published rules; not advance transition funding or same-day emergency assistance. General discharge not listed as eligible.
next_step: Review residency and service requirements, gather lease, past-due bills, DD214, income and bank statements, and apply to the Trust.
timing: Applications 1st–15th monthly; review 16th–23rd and notification 24th–end of month.

title: Hope For The Warriors — Critical Needs
description: Short-term support for urgent rent, mortgage or utility needs, with a case manager and a financial stability plan.
eligibility: Post-9/11 warrior community; provider screens financial-support criteria, including injured veterans and families, veterans experiencing homelessness and MST survivors.
caveats: Case-specific direct financial support; public page does not promise all veterans qualify. Not immediate emergency cash; published processing may take 3–4 weeks.
geographic_scope: United States / Texas grant support also noted
next_step: Use Connect to Services and request Critical Needs screening; explain expected gap between military pay and civilian/VA income.
timing: Allow 3–4 weeks for processing; begin referral early.

title: USA Cares — Military Assistance Response / Career Transition
description: Case-reviewed nonrepayable assistance for temporary service-related or medical hardship; essential expenses may also be helped during job training.
eligibility: Post-9/11 veterans, active service members and families; service-related incident or medical hardship under provider review.
caveats: Ask which housing bills qualify; not every planned transition gap qualifies. Financial education course is part of assistance application.
next_step: Use Get Help or call 800-773-0387; request Military Assistance Response screening and ask whether rent during approved job training can be considered.
help_type: Hardship grant / essential expenses during training

title: Semper Fi & America’s Fund — housing assistance (Army included)
description: Case managers may help with urgent rent, mortgage and utilities as part of recovery support for seriously wounded, ill or injured service members.
eligibility: Combat wounded, critically ill or catastrophically injured service members/veterans and military families; all-service provider, including Army.
caveats: A 30% DoD medical-retirement rating alone is not proof of meeting the Fund’s severity criteria. Case manager decides need and program eligibility.
next_step: Call 760-725-3680 or use the financial-family-assistance intake; provide diagnosis/recovery needs and housing bill.

title: VFW Financial Assistance for Service Members — apply while active
description: Grant up to $2,500 for eligible necessities; payment goes straight to the creditor. Formerly called Unmet Needs.
eligibility: Currently active duty or activated Guard/Reserve; hardship tied to eligible deployment, military pay error or pending medical discharge from service-connected injury/illness.
caveats: Current program is active-duty focused, not general post-discharge veteran rent. Requires eligible current bills and documented qualifying cause; financial mismanagement and several other causes excluded.
next_step: Call 866-789-6333 or email financialassistance@vfw.org before separation; review criteria linked on official page and ask about current rent bill.
timing: Apply while still eligible active duty; cannot assume availability after retirement.

title: Operation First Response — emergency assistance while active
description: Emergency financial support can address basics such as rent, utilities or groceries for currently serving members.
eligibility: Current emergency program serves active-duty service members of all branches; separate Gold Star/first-responder categories exist.
caveats: Provider has narrowed emergency funding to active duty. Ordinary veteran transition rent is not covered by the current general program; veteran Last Mission exception is tied to approved inpatient treatment.
next_step: Email info@operationfirstresponse.org with service member name, Army status, hardship summary and phone; no public application window.
timing: Contact before separation for an actual current emergency; provider reviews individual need.

title: Coalition to Salute America’s Heroes — narrowly eligible emergency aid
description: Direct financial assistance for dire financial hardship in qualifying Iraq/Afghanistan combat-injured veterans.
eligibility: Post-9/11 OEF/OIF veteran; boots on ground Iraq/Afghanistan; qualifying DD214; honorable discharge; at least 30% rating for a single injury sustained there; first-time applicant.
caveats: Combined 30% medical retirement or a noncombat injury does not establish eligibility. Limited funds; general discharge not accepted in published criteria.
next_step: Review every eligibility condition and use online intake if met; if excluded, ask about advocacy referrals.

title: HUD–VASH — longer-term supportive rental voucher
description: Rental voucher paired with VA case management to help eligible homeless veterans sustain permanent housing.
eligibility: VA homelessness/case-management eligibility and housing-authority income screening; local VA and housing authority determine admission.
caveats: Not routine rent for every separating Soldier and not an automatic near-homelessness benefit. Voucher availability, referral and housing search can take time.
next_step: Ask the destination VA homeless coordinator whether HUD–VASH or SSVF better fits your actual housing situation.

title: USAJOBS — federal veterans’ preference
description: Eligible veterans receive hiring consideration under federal preference rules. Find federal jobs and claim the correct preference on your application.
eligibility: Honorable or general discharge plus qualifying service, campaign, Purple Heart or service-connected disability criteria.
caveats: Military service alone does not always qualify. Rules vary by hiring authority; preference does not guarantee a job. Submit DD-214, SF-15 and rating evidence as applicable. Active members may use qualifying certification of expected discharge.
geographic_scope: U.S. / overseas federal jobs; filter DMV, Houston or remote
next_step: Create your USAJOBS profile, review the veterans hiring path, and save location-specific searches.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Federal hiring — 30% or more disabled veteran authority
description: A federal agency may appoint a qualified disabled veteran without the usual competitive process, with no grade ceiling.
eligibility: Military retirement with service-connected disability of at least 30%, OR a compensable VA service-connected rating of at least 30%; honorable/general discharge documentation.
caveats: Agency discretion; no guaranteed appointment. DoD and VA ratings are different, but either documented qualifying route can work. Initial time-limited appointment must exceed 60 days; conversion is discretionary.
geographic_scope: U.S. / federal jobs; useful for DMV
next_step: Once documented, tell agency HR you qualify and provide VA letter or military retirement/discharge evidence.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Federal hiring — Veterans Recruitment Appointment (VRA)
description: Agencies can hire eligible veterans noncompetitively into qualifying positions through GS-11 or equivalent.
eligibility: Qualifying disabled, campaign/expeditionary-medal, Armed Forces Service Medal or recently separated veterans; honorable/general discharge.
caveats: Must meet position qualifications. Agency decides whether to use VRA. Permanent-track appointments convert after two satisfactory years; temporary/term appointments do not carry that conversion.
next_step: Ask the agency veterans employment coordinator about VRA and provide qualifying discharge/award documents.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Army PaYS — guaranteed partner interviews
description: Army partner employers offer qualifying Soldiers job interviews and possible employment after service.
eligibility: Current Army Soldiers may register retroactively; PaYS Live includes Soldiers within 18 months of exit and Army veterans. Honorable discharge required.
caveats: Interview guarantee is subject to program/partner requirements; employment is not guaranteed. General discharge is not the published qualifying discharge.
next_step: Register for PaYS Reservations and PaYS Live now; search partners near Houston and the DMV.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Hiring Our Heroes — Corporate Fellowship
description: A 12-week civilian workplace fellowship helps you gain experience and meet potential employers before leaving active duty.
eligibility: Active-duty transitioning members with aligned timeline, education and leadership experience; program within last 180 days, subject to Army approval.
caveats: Army rank/service limits and command approval may shorten the authorized window. Cohort and employer selection are competitive; no job guarantee.
geographic_scope: Nationwide; host locations and remote options vary
next_step: Contact your Army CSP office immediately, then attend the fellowship information session and confirm cohort timing.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Amazon / AWS — paid technical apprenticeships
description: Paid classroom and hands-on training helps veterans move into cloud technology careers, followed by up to 12 months of paid on-the-job training.
eligibility: Military veterans; individual apprenticeship requirements apply.
caveats: Cohorts and roles vary. No guaranteed opening in Houston, DMV or remotely; employer recruitment is not statutory veterans’ preference.
next_step: Follow the official apprenticeship page to current openings and check location and start dates.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Amazon — military career recruiting
description: Military-focused recruiting connects your Army experience to operations, logistics, technology and other civilian roles.
eligibility: Veterans, transitioning active service members, Guard and Reserve; role requirements apply.
caveats: Recruiting commitment does not guarantee preference, an interview or employment. Check each posting for location and credentials.
next_step: Use the military careers portal and filter openings for Houston, DMV or remote.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Lockheed Martin — Continuing Your Mission / Heroes
description: Military relations managers help match experience to roles; the Heroes program includes internships, fellowships and SkillBridge opportunities.
eligibility: Transitioning service members and veterans; each program and position has its own requirements.
caveats: No guaranteed interview or statutory preference. SkillBridge needs Army approval before separation; clearance and citizenship requirements may apply.
next_step: Enroll in Continuing Your Mission and ask the military relations team about Heroes and your separation date.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Northrop Grumman — SkillBridge
description: On-the-job civilian training during the end of active service in engineering, cyber, manufacturing and related work.
eligibility: At least 180 days active service; company asks applicants within 12 months of separation/retirement, expected honorable discharge, transition/ethics training and commander authorization.
caveats: Actual participation occurs during the final authorized service window, up to 180 days, with Army-specific limits. Selection and a later job are not guaranteed.
next_step: Join the military talent network, mark your resume SkillBridge Eligible, and coordinate dates with Army CSP.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Northrop Grumman — military recruiting and Operation IMPACT
description: Military career matching and a talent network connect veterans to roles. Operation IMPACT supports separating members with service-connected conditions.
eligibility: Veterans and transitioning service members; Operation IMPACT has additional program screening.
caveats: A prospective 30% rating does not automatically establish Operation IMPACT eligibility. Ask for its current criteria. No guaranteed preference or job.
geographic_scope: U.S.; check DMV and other locations
next_step: Join the military talent community and ask whether Operation IMPACT fits your medical transition.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: BAE Systems — military recruiting / Warrior Integration
description: Veteran recruiters and an Army MOS translator help identify roles. Warrior Integration provides specialized training for post-9/11 members with service-connected injuries.
eligibility: Veterans and transitioning service members; Warrior Integration and positions have separate criteria.
caveats: Private employer pathway, not statutory preference. General-discharge eligibility and disability criteria must be confirmed per program; no automatic admission.
next_step: Use the MOS translator and military interest form; ask about Warrior Integration and roles in the DMV.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: BAE Systems — SkillBridge
description: Civilian work experience and training during the last part of active service, with possible full-time employment afterward.
eligibility: Active-duty members able to finish within their last 180 days and obtain branch/command approval.
caveats: Army limits may reduce duration. Company lists specific locations; do not assume a Houston or DMV placement. Selection and employment are not guaranteed.
geographic_scope: Selected U.S. sites; current needs vary
next_step: Apply to a matching role and submit the SkillBridge interest form with your preferred region.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Booz Allen — military recruiting / HOH fellowship
description: Military talent recruiting and a 12-week Hiring Our Heroes fellowship help translate service experience into civilian work.
eligibility: Transitioning active-duty members for the service-member fellowship route; veterans can pursue regular military recruiting.
caveats: Confirm the correct HOH route and Army approval. Roles may require citizenship or clearances. Employer support is not statutory preference or a job guarantee.
geographic_scope: U.S. / overseas; check DMV and role-specific remote options
next_step: Explore military careers, join the talent community and ask HOH about a cohort matching your exit date.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Wells Fargo — National Military Apprenticeship
description: One- or two-year registered apprenticeships hire participants as full-time employees with pay and benefits from day one.
eligibility: U.S. military veterans of all eras, Guard and Reserve; position qualifications apply.
caveats: Roles post throughout the year and locations vary; relocation may be required. VA education benefits require separate eligibility. No job guarantee.
next_step: Join the military talent community and check current apprenticeship postings for desired locations.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Hire Heroes USA — free career coaching
description: A career advisor helps with civilian resumes, interviews, networking, job searches and salary negotiation at no charge.
eligibility: Transitioning members and veterans of all service eras; discharge received or expected must be above dishonorable.
caveats: Career support, not a placement agency or guaranteed job. Provider recommends registering within 18 months of availability to work.
next_step: Register now with service documentation and your expected separation date.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: RecruitMilitary — veteran jobs and career fairs
description: A military-focused job board and in-person/virtual fairs connect you with employers recruiting veterans, including overseas roles.
eligibility: Transitioning members, veterans, Guard and Reserve; each opening has separate requirements.
caveats: A veteran-focused listing is not proof of statutory hiring preference. Event and vacancy availability changes.
geographic_scope: Nationwide / virtual / overseas; filter Houston or DMV
next_step: Build your profile and search by Army MOS, city or remote; check the live fair calendar.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: HIRE Vets Medallion — employer directory
description: Find employers recognized by the Department of Labor for veteran hiring, retention and professional development.
eligibility: Directory open to everyone; individual jobs have their own requirements.
caveats: An award identifies employer practices, not a guaranteed preference, current vacancy or interview. Check award year and each company career page.
geographic_scope: All states; filter Texas, Maryland, Virginia or DC
next_step: Filter the map by location, then check the awardees’ official career sites.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Maryland American Job Centers — veteran employment help
description: Local job centers provide job-search help; qualifying veterans receive priority of service, and eligible veterans can receive intensive employment support.
eligibility: Transitioning members and veterans; priority and Disabled Veterans Outreach Program eligibility require screening.
caveats: Priority is access to qualifying services, not guaranteed employer preference or job placement. A Maryland license alone does not settle program eligibility.
next_step: Contact the center near your intended Maryland home and ask for a veteran employment intake.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: DC government — veterans’ hiring preference
description: Eligible veterans may claim legal hiring preference when applying for qualifying District government positions.
eligibility: Qualifying disabled veterans or veterans with eligible service periods/operations; proof required with application.
caveats: Retirees at Major/Lieutenant Commander or above generally excluded unless retirement is service-connected disability based. Verify the posting and current eligibility with DCHR; a job is not guaranteed.
next_step: Read the preference requirements and attach service/disability proof with the application.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Virginia state jobs — veterans’ hiring preference
description: Qualified veterans receive added hiring consideration; service-connected disabled veterans receive additional preference.
eligibility: Qualifying veterans who meet the job’s minimum requirements; disability preference uses a VA service-connected rating.
caveats: Preference does not guarantee selection. Virginia’s rules differ from federal hiring; follow state documentation requirements.
next_step: Claim veteran status on the state application and provide requested discharge and VA rating evidence.
verification: Service / disability documents or employer application

title: Microsoft Cleared Talent Accelerator — 90-day training
description: Free full-time remote technology training for transitioning service members and veterans who already hold an active TS/SCI clearance or higher.
eligibility: Active TS/SCI or higher; learning-path prerequisites and relevant experience; Army approval for SkillBridge.
caveats: No clearance sponsorship or guaranteed job. Cloud/consulting path requires at least one year of relevant IT experience. Applications roll until capacity; provider says accepting applications, but individual seats are not confirmed.
next_step: Review eligibility and apply through the portal linked on Microsoft’s official page.
timing: Cloud/consulting cohort February 22–May 21, 2027. Project-management applications begin November 16, 2026.
